key_idea: The answer is the maximum over all prefixes of (largest letter count - smallest letter count).
sketch: Lower bound: in any prefix each beautiful subsequence contributes counts of A,B,C that differ by at most 1, so at least max-min subsequences are needed. Upper bound: a greedy that always appends a letter to an open subsequence whose current triple lacks it (opening a new one only when forced) achieves it. So just scan once keeping three counters and the running max of max-min, O(n). Verified against an exhaustive DP over subsequence states for all random strings up to length 12.
